[[File:Small ditrigonal dodecacronic hexecontahedron.stl|thumb|3D model of a small ditrigonal dodecacronic hexecontahedron]]
In [[geometry]], the '''small ditrigonal dodecacronic hexecontahedron''' (or '''fat star''') is a nonconvex [[Isohedral figure|isohedral]] [[polyhedron]]. It is the [[Dual polyhedron|dual]] of the [[uniform star polyhedron|uniform]] [[small ditrigonal dodecicosidodecahedron]]. It is visually identical to the [[small dodecicosacron]]. Its faces are darts. A part of each dart lies inside the solid, hence is invisible in solid models.

== Proportions ==
Faces have two angles of <math>\arccos(\frac{5}{12}+\frac{1}{4}\sqrt{5})\approx 12.661\,078\,804\,43^{\circ}</math>, one of <math>\arccos(-\frac{5}{12}-\frac{1}{60}\sqrt{5})\approx 116.996\,396\,851\,70^{\circ}</math> and one of <math>360^{\circ}-\arccos(-\frac{1}{12}-\frac{19}{60}\sqrt{5})\approx 217.681\,445\,539\,45^{\circ}</math>. Its [[dihedral angles]] equal <math>\arccos({\frac{-44-3\sqrt{5}}{61}})\approx 146.230\,659\,755\,53^{\circ}</math>. The ratio between the lengths of the long and short edges is <math>\frac{31+5\sqrt{5}}{38}\approx 1.110\,008\,944\,41</math>.
